Ribot discusses his intent to challenge that instrument’s conventional prettiness. One classical-guitar role and zero singers are retained. The creator-owned Sound of Tzadik playlist positively includes Marc Ribot. The label itself describes an international experimental composer community; the selected release is positively on Tzadik and is a complete solo study collection. The category is not equated with Jewish jazz, free jazz, or the broad classical guitar instrument category. Contemporary artMusic.westernModern is a selected composed experimental-study branch, not a category-wide assertion. Authored spruce top, fan bracing, normal nylon strings and fingerpicked free-stroke touch are practical neutral construction/playing choices, not a Thomas Humphrey model reconstruction or an exhaustive transcription of each study’s gestures. extras.description: Cynthia Lin’s own March2016 public post publishes her Moon River fingerpicking tutorial and attaches the matching ukulele chart. The complete one-page chart credits her arrangement of Mancini/Mercer, supplies lyrics, chord sequence and a four-string fingerpicking pattern. Its defined vocal-and-ukulele teaching realization is retained as one authored singer accompanying themselves on one ukulele. This is a realization of the full published chart, not an assertion that all versions of her2017 album recording have this personnel. The creator-owned Ukulele Cover playlist item37 is Cynthia Lin Moon River, positively tying the exact artist/song to the cover cluster. The category concerns adaptations of existing repertoire for ukulele, narrower than the broad instrument category Ukulele and not identical to Hawaiian folk or original ukulele compositions. The artist’s own tutorial and published full lyric/chord arrangement establish a complete permissible educational scope; the singer count is an explicit one-person realization of the source chart, not an inferred actual session count. No backing band, added harmony singers or original film orchestra is copied into this chart realization. BalladPoetry covers the selected minimally accompanied song interpretation. Fingerpicked style is source-supported; concert-size mahogany ukulele and unprocessed single voice are authored practical choices rather than claims of the instrument in the video. Source chart says3/4 while own index calls it6/8; no measured meter is pinned here and this discrepancy is disclosed rather than silently settled. Educational chart and original credits were consulted only for factual arrangement structure; no lyrics or score are redistributed. The broad city category is distinct from Uppsala/Stockholm indie and from nationwide Swedish indie; it includes but is not synonymous with generic stoner or psychedelic rock. Voice physiology remains unspecified; solo-accompanied single lead refers to the one named singer, not three band members as choir. Photo is LOW recording-microphone context only. extras.description: Jayanthi Kumaresh — Mysterious Duality, complete four-track EarthSync album (label digital edition2013). One performer overlays seven different Saraswati veenas. Artist and label explicitly say only veena; all lead, rhythmic, drone and percussive layers derive from these instruments. Composers Abhishek Raghuram and R.Kumaresh are not additional credited performers. No sung voice, drum, tambura or synth is imported. Veena is the instrument-centred recorded repertoire category, narrower than all Carnatic music and broader than any one playing lineage. This documented layered Carnatic compositional branch differs from purely vocal Carnatic, rudra-veena dhrupad and slide-guitar mohan-veena repertoires; no whole-category equivalence is asserted. ArtMusic.southAsian reflects explicitly codified raga/tala and Carnatic compositional grammar, not guessed free improvisation. One existing Saraswati-veena card aggregates a single sounding family while retaining seven source instruments and their full lead/rhythm/drone/percussive roles in evidence; it does not claim literal one-layer reconstruction. Joined jackwood construction, gourd resonator, steel/bronze strings, wire plucking and Thanjavur rendering are authored coherent defaults, not measured seven-instrument hardware nor exclusive artist lineage. Shared technique provides an ornamented-melodic emphasis; prose preserves additional documented layered functions without inventing separate drums. Global tuning omitted because exact four-work raga/pitch configuration not supplied by selected sources.

extras.description: Archival album record identifies five whale recordings: Solo Whale, its slowed-down version, Tower Whales, Distant Whale and Three Whale Trip; field recordists are Frank Watlington and Roger and Katharine Payne. Complete five-track environmental album scope, including its explicitly slowed version; not human music layered over whale calls. No human singers or instrumental accompaniment are credited. tradition.lineage: Nofinishi Dywili — Umagungqel’indawo, complete SAMRO transcribed voice-and-uhadi performance. Representative authored present-day recording arrangement for the selected documented branch. Sources establish category, roles and locality. extras.description: SAMRO’s Indigenous African Music project publishes this complete transcription from Nofinishi Dywili’s performance for one voice and uhadi. Its contextual notes identify a Xhosa beer song about social position, with the lyric and bow lines retained throughout. The selected lineage is Eastern Cape Xhosa song, distinct from spoken praise poetry, hip hop or umngqokolo overtone singing. Complete documented intimate voice-and-bow branch, not a claim that the whole Xhosa music category has one ensemble. Song-poetry priority and minimal accompaniment justify balladPoetry. The uhadi owner preserves attached gourd, single struck string and chest-facing resonance without mislabeling it a mouth bow or requiring overtone vocal production. Source material remains unspecified because the institution allows gut or wire. One notated voice and one bow line are not a choir. No equal-temperament tuning is imposed on this indigenous bow practice. Lady Frere is the documented nearby locality of the artist’s home Ngqoko, not a claimed recording address. extras.description: Smithsonian credits Hussein Ali-Hijazi alone on lead vocals for the 4:57 Ghazal excerpt in Yemen: Traditional Music of the North. The original liner notes identify a love-and-friendship poem and describe solo domestic strophic singing in Saadah, where this tradition excludes instrumental accompaniment. This complete published excerpt therefore retains one unaccompanied singer; it is not presented as the entire longer gathering. Voice tradition, register and technique remain source-unspecified; modern clean recording choices are authored rather than historical session reconstruction. Tuning is intentionally omitted. Yoga as intended practice differs from general background music and meditation without asserting disjoint listener uses. Five named singers retain group singing; exact arrangement of soprano/alto/tenor lines is not encoded as a measured choral transcription. Lagos is a production-network locality documented by the studio naming Dare Justified as a client, not the medley recording address. tradition.lineage: Haustor — Mijenjam se, Zagreb Music Biennale15May1981, complete documented concert lineup. extras.description: Croatia Records documents the1981 Zagreb performance and its2025 restored single. The complete named lineup is Darko Rundek voice/guitar, Srđan Sacher bass, Srđan Gulić Gul drums, Damir Prica-Capri saxophone, Ozren Štiglić guitar and Zoran Vuletić keyboards. One credited singer and all five instrumental families are retained, including both guitarists within one family card. The label describes punk-charged playing; Sacher explicitly identifies their rhythm section with the new wave. The creator-owned Yugoslav New Wave playlist positively names Haustor at items4/68, while the issuing label independently places this historical performance in the new-wave scene. This historical cross-Yugoslav new-wave cluster is narrower than Yugoslav rock generally and is not identical to later Croatian indie or all post-punk. The selected complete concert lineup is not a generic band lineup projected onto an unrelated album; no credited keyboard or saxophone is omitted. Saxophone is realized with authored alto/medium-reed/hard-rubber settings, not a claim of source subtype or maker. Keyboards retain unspecified electronic architecture. Electric single-coil overdriven lead guitar, fingerstyle electric bass and stick kit are authored present-day realizations of the source rock palette. The original partly missing recording channels are a restoration limitation, not permission to remove players. Current digital recording settings do not reconstruct the1981 recording chain. DistortedRock.punk covers the explicitly punk-charged/post-punk branch selected here without forcing the Anglosphere ancestry of the catalog’s popRock.newWave node. tradition.name: Yunnan Traditional
tradition.lineage: Ellie Mao and Anna Mi Lee — complete three-song Yunnan section, An Anthology of Chinese Folk Songs (1963), tracks204–206. Authored present-day recording arrangement based on the documented selected performance branch. Sources support category, credited roles and locality. Materials, makes, technique presets, tuning, studio, signal chain and axes are authored realizations, not measured historical session settings or universal genre rules.

extras.description: Smithsonian Folkways identifies a contiguous complete Yunnan section: My Love Is Like a Dragon in the Sky, The Mule-Driver’s Song and The Guessing Song, tracks204–206. Each track’s primary performer metadata credits Ellie Mao lead vocals and Anna Mi Lee piano. One singer and one piano accompany the complete three regional songs. Smithsonian identifies the selected tracks with Chinese language; no narrower ethnicity is imposed across all three. The Museum of Chinese in America, documenting its copy and inserts, explicitly describes a contemporary Mandarin-language and piano-accompanied presentation of inherited regional folk songs. The Yunnan source-repertoire boundary, not convenient instrumentation, determines the three-track selection; all three named Yunnan songs in this anthology are retained. Other provinces are not silently relabeled Yunnan. This is the documented folk-song concert-arrangement branch of the broad Yunnan traditional category, not an assertion that all Yunnan minority traditions or original village practice use piano or Mandarin. The positive institutional regional-folk identification supports category directly; no creator-map membership is invented. Yunnan is more specific than the whole Chinese traditional category and differs from neighboring Sichuan/Tibetan traditions; regional and ethnic practices may overlap. BalladPoetry expresses inherited lyrical songs with one accompaniment and does not force Western classical ancestry merely because the piano is present. Authored SteinwayD nine-foot grand with legato support, modern action, standard pitch and recording chain are present-day realization choices, not claims about the1963 instrument or original folk tuning. No jaw harp, flute, string ensemble or second singer is added from other recordings. Authored present-day recording arrangement based on the documented selected performance branch. Sources support category, credited roles and locality. extras.description: Smithsonian Festival of American Folklife1997 pp63–66 documents Mokhukhu communal singing and prayer with rhythmic heavy-white-boot stamps, among male members of Edward’s Zion Christian Church at Moria. It explicitly distinguishes this formation from the church’s female choir, male choir, brass band and Nkedi. The selected documented song-and-stamp practice retains group voice and foot percussion; the article does not give a headcount, fixed Western choral voicing, instrumentation for a commercial recording, or a tuning measurement. The creator-owned ZCC playlist positively lists ZCC Mokhukhu with Z.C.C. Choir at item17, corroborating this selected formation inside its broader Zionist gospel cluster. The selected ethnographic practice is not projected onto that commercial Mpoho recording, whose session personnel are not documented here. ZCC is a particular Zionist church-associated musical cluster, not an alias for all South African gospel, isicathamiya, or Western black-gospel choir. This entry realizes the Moria article’s documented communal voice and boot-stamp branch, not every ZCC formation and not a claim that the church uses no instruments. Other congregations or performances may add rhythm makers; the separate Marabastad fieldwork account describes staff/whip rhythmic contact and is not silently treated as the same precisely scoped performance. Heavy boots are positively documented; an earth-ground surface, unprocessed live-group recording, local singing articulation left unspecified, and twelve-tone studio pitch reference are explicitly authored present-day realization choices rather than ethnographic measurement. The source does not state individual singer count or impose SATB; no fabricated four-person count is used. RitualDevotional preserves the article’s stated prayer-and-worship function. extras.description: The issuing label identifies this2011 Zillertal/Tyrol folk-pop release and lists its complete trio: Freddy Pfister accordion, keyboard and voice; Daniel Grissemann Steirische Harmonika, bass and voice; Andreas Innerbichler guitar, keyboard and voice. All three credited singers and all five instrumental families are retained, including the two distinct free-reed roles. The palette is the release-level union, not a claim of simultaneous performance on every track. Creator-owned The Sound of Zillertal lists Freddy Pfister Band at item43. This geographically focused Alpine folk-pop discovery category is narrower than pan-Alpine Volksmusik and distinct from Alpenpanorama as a separate classifier cluster; no disjoint repertoire boundary is claimed. Selected modern trio scope does not stand for every valley ensemble or add instruments from generic Volksmusik. FunctionalSong is an explicit authored verse/refrain and functional-chord realization of the vocal folk-pop branch within this mixed song/dance release; it is not a measured structural claim for its instrumental polkas. Neutral electronic-keyboard owner retains source-unspecified generator architecture. Generic accordion is authored dry LMM steel-reed, while Steirische is authored four-row helicon-bass; one shared folk technique is valid for both. Source guitar and bass are realized as strummed steel-string dreadnought and fingerstyle electric bass, explicitly authored choices rather than documented source construction. No drummer, brass, zither or sampled backing is invented. Authored present-day recording arrangement based on the documented selected performance branch.
